2026-08-21T12:30:59.9917413Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9918171Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9918797Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9919755Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9920484Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9921464Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9924599Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9928060Z >
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9932807Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9937629Z >
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9939220Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9940727Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9941099Z ### How to Use
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9941571Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9943043Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9944510Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9944874Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9945921Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9947409Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9948650Z ```
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9949109Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9949594Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9950727Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9951995Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9953590Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9955280Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9956774Z ```
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9957189Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9958349Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9960069Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9961194Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9962734Z ```
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9963158Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9963764Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9965141Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9966224Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9967955Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9969363Z ```
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9969790Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9970319Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9971162Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9974167Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9977414Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9977768Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9978681Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9980357Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9982149Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9982790Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9983671Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9985678Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9988057Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9990379Z ```
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9990821Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9992569Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9994416Z 
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9994767Z ```bash
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9996151Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9998021Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-21T12:30:59.9999452Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0000303Z 
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0001102Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0002911Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0004026Z ```
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0004459Z 
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0004892Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0006446Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0008365Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0010289Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0012446Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0014530Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0015596Z 
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0015964Z ### Notes
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0016396Z 
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0017620Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0020427Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0023093Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0025557Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0027932Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0030062Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0032204Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-21T12:31:00.0033586Z </mcp-clis>
